subject: Re: Urgent — EmberField production latency tsunami / routing ask
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@emberfield.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, support@emberfield.com
Cc: priya.rao@emberfield.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2029 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: high error rate + latency spike in us-west-2 (az-b)

Irene / Redwood ops team —

We started seeing a huge latency spike and 502/504 errors across the EmberField production fleet targeting us-west-2 AZ-b around 15:40 PDT. A sizeable portion of our traffic is timing out (50–60% failure on NGINX) and response times for successful calls jumped from ~120ms to 3–6s. Our customers are experiencing timeouts on critical workflows.

Attached is a tar of NGINX + application logs and one screenshot from our monitoring that shows the spike. We urgently need one of the following:

- Temporary cross-region failover (route our prod traffic to us-east-1) OR
- Immediate traffic diversion to a stable AZ in us-west-2 if available, plus a commitment on timeline to restore capacity

This is P0 for us. Please advise next steps and whether an exec-level escalation is required.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Ops, EmberField

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: daniel.park@emberfield.com, priya.rao@emberfield.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2029 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: high error rate + latency spike in us-west-2 (az-b) — initial triage

Irene / team — quick triage notes (observed in our telemetry):

- Confirmed: spike in 5xx and tail latency centered on us-west-2 AZ-b starting ~15:36 PDT.
- Symptoms: elevated queue depth on several inference pools, KV cache pressure on large-seq models, intermittent DB connectivity timeouts from local metadata store (timeout 2s -> 6s).
- Impact: roughly 40–55% of EmberField’s sessions to us-west-2 are experiencing timeouts; other regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1) look nominal.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Geo-rehome EmberField traffic to us-east-1 — recommended if EmberField can accept the brief consistency window and slightly higher RTT for some users. We can do a staged cut-over (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on elevated errors. Estimated time to first traffic flip: 18–25 minutes if approved.
2) AZ drain inside us-west-2 (move traffic from AZ-b -> AZ-c) — only viable if their capacity footprint is small and us-west-2 AZ-c health is confirmed. This is faster but riskier if there’s region-level degradation.
3) Model-level fallback to smaller quantized variant in AZ-b to reduce KV pressure — will reduce quality and requires customer approval.

Risks for option 1 (geo-rehome): increased tail latency for APAC users and ephemeral cache warmup leading to token-cost spike. We should coordinate cookie/session routing and advise customer about short-lived errors during cut-over window.

Irene — I’ll open INF-3291, start a cross-team bridge, and queue the runbook. Vanessa/Rishi — if you want an exec bridge with customer leadership, say so; I’ll also prepare an action checklist for the on-call to execute the staged flip.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE, Regional Routing
Redwood Inference

Related: JIRA INF-3291

I want the account team on the call to offer transparent remediation and to capture any ask for credits. Rishi — can you prepare a one-time credit recommendation (range and precedent) in case the customer pushes on commercial impact?

Irene, I’ll join the bridge and lead the customer comms. Hannah — prioritize the staged 5% -> 25% -> 100% flow and the rollback trigger (>=10% increase in errors or >=2x latency). Keep the runbook steps minimal and scriptable.

Vanessa Ortiz

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: daniel.park@emberfield.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2029 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: commercial prep for EmberField rehome request

Vanessa — quick commercial stance: EmberField is on an annual committed plan (HS-98765). Given the customer impact and the short-term nature of the mitigation, my initial recommendation is:

- Offer a goodwill credit equal to one week of variable usage (estimated range $6k–$10k) if we execute the geo-rehome within the SLA window.
- If the incident extends >48 hours due to platform fault, escalate to 2x the above credit and consider a short-term capacity uplift at no charge.

I’ll draft wording for the bridge and the postmortem comms. Irene — let me know if EmberField leadership insists on a larger commercial concession during the call.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: daniel.park@emberfield.com, priya.rao@emberfield.com

Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2029 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — EmberField production latency tsunami / routing ask — next steps

Daniel / Priya — thank you for the prompt details and logs. Quick summary of the plan we executed and next steps: 

1) At 09:58 PDT we initiated a staged geo-rehome of EmberField production traffic from us-west-2 to us-east-1: 5% traffic shift -> monitor 10 minutes -> 25% -> 100%. All stages passed the error/latency rollback thresholds. Full cut-over completed at 10:21 PDT.
2) Impact observed post-cut: error rate dropped to baseline (<1.5%), median latency for EmberField ~210ms in us-east-1. We saw a brief cache-warmup cost increase but no client-visible regressions after 10:30 PDT.
3) Hannah has opened INF-3291 for deeper root cause (KV pressure + AZ-b metadata store timeouts). We will provide a detailed postmortem and remediation plan within 72 hours.
4) Commercial: Rishi proposed a one-week variable-usage credit; Vanessa will confirm and include final wording in the post-incident comms.

We understand this was disruptive — Vanessa/Rishi and I will join an executive bridge at 11:00 PDT if you want to discuss details and next steps. Please confirm a preferred bridge format (Zoom/phone) and any additional folks to include.

Irene Choi
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
